children: Chainalysis says its new AI investigation tool helped trace billions of dollars in crypto stolen from Binance. The funds moved across nearly a dozen blockchains.

The heist drained approximately $6.4 billion from Binance's hot wallets on October 29, 2026. That makes it the largest single theft the crypto sector has recorded. The attackers moved fast, and the investigators needed to move faster.
The attack began at 4:20 p.m. ET. Most of the money left Binance within a roughly 20-minute window.
Chainalysis ran its investigation using Chain, an AI-native workspace the firm built for blockchain investigators. The analysis pointed to TraderTraitor, a hacking group linked to North Korea.

The attribution rests on on-chain evidence. Stolen Binance funds were commingled with proceeds from an earlier exploit of Bitget in September 2026, just weeks before. Mixing loot from two jobs is efficient for the thieves. It also leaves a fingerprint.
The laundering playbook was described as unprecedented. It involved thousands of recursive transactions, with funds cycled rapidly through a long chain of blockchain addresses.
One oddly specific detail stood out. Many of those transaction sequences started with exactly 1 TRX on the Tron blockchain.

Exchanges and stablecoin issuers moved to lock down what they could. As of early November 2026, approximately $2.8 billion had been frozen through that coordinated effort. Binance estimated the frozen total could reach as high as $3 billion.
The hackers clearly understood how freezes work. Stablecoins like USDT and USDC have issuers that can blacklist addresses and lock tokens in place. Ether has no such central switch.

So the attackers swapped around $325 million in stablecoins for about $285 million in ETH, and they did it in roughly 20 minutes. They accepted a noticeably worse rate to get out of assets that could be frozen.
Chainalysis publicly launched Chain on November 19, 2026. The company pointed to the Binance investigation as a showcase for what the tool can do.

The firm is pitching Chain on real-time monitoring and automated workflows. The idea is to let investigators follow illicit funds across different blockchains without manually stitching together each hop.

TraderTraitor's alleged involvement fits a pattern that investigators have flagged before. North Korea-linked groups have been tied to major crypto thefts, and the Bitget connection suggests this crew was active across multiple targets in a short span.

The commingling evidence also cut both ways. It helped Chainalysis link the two incidents. But it signals a group confident enough to run proceeds from separate hacks through shared infrastructure, apparently without much fear of the connection being drawn.

For stablecoin issuers, the case is a partial win. Their freeze powers helped lock up a large share of the recovered funds. Yet the $325 million conversion into ETH shows exactly where that tool runs out. Once money leaves a freezable asset, the issuer's leverage disappears.
Attackers are automating their laundering, as the thousands of recursive transactions show. Investigators are automating their tracing, as Chain is meant to do.

title: Chainalysis traces billions stolen in Binance hack with its new AI tool
